planting.note: Plant container-grown vines in spring against a sheltered wall, fence, or trellis so stems can begin twining before cool weather returns.

directions: This older selection, traced to seed collected in central China in the early twentieth century, is distinguished from standard star jasmine by narrower, smaller leaves with pronounced silvery veining that flush bronze and deepen to crimson through winter cold. It climbs more vigorously than the species type, twining tightly onto wire, lattice, or masonry, and still produces the same clusters of small, intensely fragrant white pinwheel flowers in summer. Give it full sun to light shade and well-drained soil, water regularly the first year to establish a strong root system, and prune after bloom only as needed to redirect growth, since flowers form on the current season's wood. Winter foliage color is most vivid where nights turn cold but the plant itself stays evergreen.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger passes; light shade helps preserve the brightest variegation through the hottest part of summer.

directions: A patented sport prized for thick, leathery leaves marbled in yellow and cream over green, with brightness that intensifies in part shade and mellows in strong sun depending on soil and season. Growth is somewhat less vigorous and more mounding than plain star jasmine, making it workable as a trained climber on a modest trellis or left to spill as a colorful groundcover. Plant in loose, well-drained soil, water regularly while establishing, and expect the usual flush of small fragrant white flowers in summer alongside the variegated foliage display. Light shearing after bloom keeps the plant dense and encourages fresh variegated growth.

planting.note: Install in spring on a trellis, arbor, or fence where the sweet root-beer-like fragrance of the late-spring flowers can be enjoyed up close.

directions: Grown chiefly for its unusually strong, sweet root-beer-scented flower clusters that open profusely over a long late-spring to early-summer season, distinguishing it from the more generically jasmine-scented forms of star jasmine. The vine climbs with the same twining habit as the species and needs a support structure to reach its full height, or can be kept clipped lower as an informal screen. It tolerates heat, salt spray, and brief drought once established, and performs best in full sun with regular water during the first growing season. Trim lightly after flowering to maintain shape and encourage branching.
